It further explores how testimonial, hermeneutical, and appropriative justice could operate across the full research-to-practice pipeline and offers concrete, stage-by-stage guidance for graduate educators, researchers, journal editors, practitioners, and organizational leaders who want their work to be both rigorous and just.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1826790\", \"pmid\": \"42661634\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13518155\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1826790\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13518155\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13518155?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"One Health: An epistemological genealogy.\", \"abstract\": \"The concept of One Health is commonly framed as an integrative model linking human, animal, and environmental health. While this articulation has been essential for policy development and institutional alignment, it remains descriptive mainly and can obscure the paradigm's epistemological foundations. This article argues that One Health should be understood not merely as a coordination framework, but as the contemporary consolidation of a long-standing interdisciplinary mode of knowing health. Using a genealogical approach, we trace convergent lines of thought across philosophy, ecology, medicine and veterinary science, public health, nursing, and social sciences. Across these traditions, recurring commitments emerge: health as relational and situated; causality as multi-level, non-linear, and distributed across human-animal-environment interactions; and ethical responsibility toward the ecological conditions that sustain life. Recognising this lineage reframes One Health as a way of knowing: one that requires concepts, methods, and responsibilities commensurate with entangled human-animal-environment realities.\", \"doi\": \"10.1016/j.onehlt.2026.101524\", \"pmid\": \"42571260\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13451898\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/j.onehlt.2026.101524\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13451898\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13451898?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"The Remission Therapy Inquiry-Based Research Model (RIRM): a conceptual framework for mechanistic hypothesis generation.\", \"abstract\": \"

Background

Modern biomedical research excels at validating hypotheses but often struggles with conceptual discovery. The emphasis on statistical significance has fostered a culture of measurement without mechanism-abundant evidence, yet limited progress toward durable restoration of health. The Remission Therapy Inquiry-Based Research Model (RIRM) was developed to address this gap by reframing how scientists reason about the mechanisms through which biological systems achieve functional coherence and recovery.

Concept

In RIRM, True Remission is used not as a biological endpoint but as a conceptual lens for mechanistic inquiry. The framework guides researchers to identify the mechanistic origins of clinical phenomena-whether cellular, molecular, systemic, adaptive, or emergent through interacting biological systems-and to reason explicitly about how functional coherence may be restored. This process is organized through twelve self-inquiry questions and a route-based algorithmic roadmap that make early-stage scientific reasoning explicit, traceable, and open to examination.

Perspective

RIRM bridges qualitative and quantitative epistemologies by integrating the interpretive depth of grounded theory with the structural discipline of systems medicine. Rather than replacing empirical validation, it strengthens the conceptual foundations that precede experimentation. By shifting emphasis from the reproducibility of outcomes alone toward the transparency, coherence, and reproducibility of reasoning, RIRM positions mechanistic inquiry itself as a legitimate domain of scientific rigor in biomedical research. As a conceptual framework, it offers a structured approach for organizing, teaching, evaluating, and refining mechanistic hypotheses across multiple levels of biological interpretation.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fsysb.2026.1835804\", \"pmid\": \"42488498\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13389765\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fsysb.2026.1835804\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13389765\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13389765?pdf=render\"}]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "176f87ec9d69013b63b34acb4782ab6c2a8bdf55d02c8130717aa3a2c1063fd8", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "assumption_challenge", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1826790", "doi:10.1016/j.onehlt.2026.101524", "doi:10.3389/fsysb.2026.1835804", "pmc:PMC13670981", "pmc:PMC13518155", "pmc:PMC13451898", "pmc:PMC13389765"], "source_candidates": ["https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13670981/?tool=EBI", "https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC13670981/pdf/?tool=EBI", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13670981", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13670981?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1826790", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13518155", "https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13518155?pdf=render", "https://doi.org/10.1016/j.onehlt.2026.101524"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
